q-71914.name: Question 1
q-71914.worked_solution:
Factoring out the constant $-5$ and calculating the resulting integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int -5{e}^{x}\,\text{d}x & =-5\int {e}^{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-5{e}^{x}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

q-71910.name: Question 3
q-71910.worked_solution:
To compute the integral of a general exponential function, we just need to divide by the natural logarithm of the base of the exponential function:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {(\frac{1}{3})}^{x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{{(\frac{1}{3})}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{3})}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Using the laws of logarithms, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{3}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡1-\operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\  & =0-\operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\  & =-\operatorname{ln}⁡3.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can simplify our final answer as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{(\frac{1}{3})}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{3})}+C=-\frac{{(\frac{1}{3})}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C\end{aligned}
$$
